Monotonicity: at the first false rejection I0 is a subset of A_j, Lemma 2.1 (same draws) gives c(A_j) >= c(I0), and mu_k <= 0 gives t_k <= tau_k, so P(FWE) <= P(M_T > c(I0)). The assumptions are sufficient and stated in full (no unstated variance-consistency step is needed because assumption 1 is posed directly on the studentized maxima). New proof re-derived. c^(k)(A) is monotone in A for fixed draws (k-th largest of a superset is no smaller), so Lemma 2.1 and the closedness argument carry over. Control: let j be the step of the k-th true rejection; for every j' <= j, I' = R_{j'-1} intersect I0 has |I'| <= k-1 and I0 is a subset of A_{j'} union I', so d_{j'} >= c^(k)(A_{j'} union I') >= c^(k)(I0); each of the first k true rejections has tau_i >= t_i > c^(k)(I0), hence the k-th largest tau over I0 exceeds c^(k)(I0), giving the displayed bound; the limit step of Theorem 3.1 applies verbatim to the k-th largest. For k = 1 the rule reduces to StepM. Candidate count binom(|R_{j-1}|, k-1) is the number of maximal subsets (smaller I are dominated by monotonicity). Minor, not failed: c^(k) of a set with fewer than k elements is not defined; the natural convention -infinity keeps the proof valid.
